methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Rhoman Aerospace is a seed-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector founded by Thomas Youmans and Thomas Callen. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of seven private companies in the sector, including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air. No public comparables exist in this space, limiting the breadth of benchmarking data available.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. While five same-sector peers were identified in Drones & Autonomous, none met the minimum threshold of three comparable companies when filtered by stage, adjacent stage, or valuation tier. The seed stage within autonomous systems remains too sparsely populated at comparable scales to support reliable median-based triangulation. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity in business models, capital intensity, and development timelines across the broader peer set.

The absence of applicable quantitative methods and the thinness of stage-specific comparables create significant analytical constraints. A defensible valuation range cannot be established from the data provided. Further work would require either expanding the comp set to include earlier-stage rounds from the identified peers or employing alternative frameworks (comparable transactions, DCF) supported by target-specific financial projections and market sizing data. The primary uncertainty is the lack of seed-stage precedent in commercial drone and autonomous systems development.
